tagline: A mechanical watch you can touch

intro.title:
What is happening
behind the caseback?
intro.body: Inside {{diameter}} millimetres, about 130 parts keep a rhythm of {{beats}} beats per second.
intro.base: This tour explains the mechanism using the base {{base}}.

hint.free: Click a part · drag to rotate · scroll to zoom

home.headline:
Mechanical movements,
seen through the caseback.
home.lede: {{watches}} watches and {{calibers}} calibers, rebuilt in 3D at their real dimensions. Set the gears turning and see how they mesh.

notice.full: An unofficial educational project. Not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by any watch brand or manufacturer shown; trademarks belong to their respective owners. The 3D models are approximate reconstructions from public information and photos, and do not accurately reproduce the real watches' shape, dimensions, specifications or design.
notice.short: Unofficial and not affiliated with any brand. Models are approximate reconstructions.

contribute.title: Contribute to Caseback
contribute.body: Caseback is open source. Requesting a watch, or sending a source or correction for an estimated value, helps a lot — no code needed. Issues and PRs in English are welcome.
